newsitem.title: USA: U.S. faults New York's welfare plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. faults New York's welfare plan - paper.

text.p: Federal officials said on Monday that they had a problem with New York State's welfare plan and that New York could not get its $2.4 billion block grant until it was resolved, the New York Times said on Tuesday.
The officials told the paper that New York had not provided adequate assurance that it would comply with new federal time limits on welfare payments to families.

The state has not formally adopted the time limits set in the new federal welfare law, which prohibits federal money from being used to help any family for more than 60 months, though this period need not be consecutive.

New York State could, however, get its federal grant if Gov. George Pataki, who has submitted a sweeping new welfare plan to the state legislature, provided assurances, the paper said. The federal officials explained Pataki could take this step and revise his welfare plan after the state legislature acted.
